findings.title: Busy times are ignored on any day that has a date override
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, a slot inside a same-day date override hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` at lines 133-135, which returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. `busy` carries existing bookings and calendar busy times (packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:143-153 feeds getBusyTimes into busy, and the fixed-host call at lines 488-491 spreads it in via `...schedule`). So a booked or calendar-blocked slot on an override day is reported available again, and the invitee can double-book it. Fix: the override block should only reject slots outside the override and then fall through to the busy check, instead of returning true early. The new test at apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:788 has no busy case on an override day, so this is not covered.
findings.originReason: The early return was added by this diff. Before it, checkIfIsAvailable always reached the busy check.

verification.reason: If a slot falls inside a same-day override, every `find` callback returns undefined. `dateOverrideExist` is then true, so line 133-135 returns true before the `busy.every` check at line 153 runs. Bookings and calendar busy times (busy comes from getBusyTimes) are therefore ignored on override days.

findings.title: Two date-override ranges on the same day make every slot on that day unavailable
findings.body: packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224 creates one override per availability row with a date, with no merging, so a day with two ranges (for example 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00) yields two entries. In the `find` at lines 106-127, the callback returns truthy when a slot falls outside a same-day override (lines 117-125). For a slot in the 14:00-17:00 range, the 09:00-12:00 entry returns truthy, so `find` returns it and lines 128-131 return false. The same happens in reverse for slots in the first range. Every slot on that day is therefore rejected. packages/lib/slots.ts:210-245 still generates slots for both ranges, so the invitee sees slots that the check then removes. Fix: treat same-day overrides as a union, so a slot is available when some same-day override contains [slotStart, slotEnd].
findings.originReason: The override `find` check in checkIfIsAvailable is new in this diff.

verification.reason: getUserAvailability creates one override per dated availability row, with no merging. For a slot in one range, the other same-day override returns true from `find`, either because the slot ends before that override starts (line 118) or starts after it ends (line 123). checkIfIsAvailable then returns false, so every slot on a day with two override ranges is rejected.

findings.title: Split working hours remove every slot on that weekday, and the slot end is never checked
findings.body: packages/lib/availability.ts:92-99 pushes one WorkingHours entry per availability row, with no merging, so 'Mon 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00' becomes two Monday entries. In the `find` at lines 139-147, an entry returns true whenever the slot start falls outside its range (line 143). A 10:00 slot is therefore rejected by the 13:00-17:00 entry, and a 14:00 slot is rejected by the 09:00-12:00 entry. Both the fixed-host call (lines 488-493) and the loose-host call (lines 513-518) spread the per-user `workingHours` in, so the rejection applies on both paths. Separately, line 142 computes `end` from `slotStartTime`, the same as `start`, so the slot end is never compared with `workingHour.endTime`. Fix: a slot passes when some entry for that day has startTime <= slot start and slot end <= endTime, computed from `slotEndTime`.
findings.originReason: The working-hours check in checkIfIsAvailable was added by this diff.

verification.reason: getWorkingHours pushes a separate entry per row, and also per UTC overflow split, so one weekday can have several entries. The `find` rejects a slot if any same-day entry does not contain its start. Line 142 also computes `end` from slotStartTime, so the slot end is never checked against endTime.

findings.title: Overrides that cross midnight in the invitee's zone land on the wrong day
findings.body: The day is chosen at line 207 from the unshifted `override.start`, but the minutes are computed at lines 218-223 by shifting by `offset` and taking `.hour()*60 + .minute()`. The `.hour()` drops any day change from the shift. Example: organizer Asia/Kolkata, override 02:00 on 10 Nov, invitee Europe/London. The real instant is 9 Nov 20:30 London, but the override is selected for 10 Nov (its unshifted start is 10 Nov 02:00) and gets startTime 1230. buildSlots (lines 107-110) then emits a slot at 10 Nov 20:30 London. checkIfIsAvailable compares the override against 9 Nov (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110-111), so it finds no match, and the slot is either dropped by the working-hours check or shown on the wrong day. Fix: select the override and compute the minutes from the same shifted instant, measured from the invitee's midnight with `diff(..., 'minute')` instead of `hour()*60 + minute()`.

verification.reason: activeOverrides is chosen from the unshifted `override.start` (line 207). The new minute computation shifts by the offset but keeps only hour()*60+minute(), so a shift across midnight drops the day change. The override's time then lands on the selected (wrong) invitee day, while checkIfIsAvailable matches the override to the shifted UTC date (line 110).

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === , so the branch never runs
findings.body: Line 114 compares `dayjs(date.start).add(...)` with `dayjs(date.end).add(...)` using ===, which compares object identity, so it is always false. The branch that returns true for a zero-length override is therefore dead. If a zero-length override is meant to block the day, use `.isSame(...)` and say so. Otherwise, delete the branch.
findings.originReason: This line was added by this diff.

verification.reason: Line 114 compares two freshly built Dayjs objects with `===`, which compares object identity, so it is always false and the branch is dead.

findings.title: Same-day override match formats a local-mode date but compares it with a UTC slot date
findings.body: Line 110 calls `.format("YYYY MM DD")` on `dayjs(date.start).add(...)`, which is in local mode, while line 111 formats `slotStartTime`, which is `time.utc()` (line 100). The day match therefore depends on the server's timezone, and on a server that is not on UTC an override near midnight can match the wrong UTC date. Using `dayjs.utc(date.start)` here would make both sides UTC. I did not confirm how the server's TZ is set.
findings.originReason: This comparison is new in this diff.

verification.reason: `dayjs(date.start).add(...)` is in local mode, so `.format` uses the server's timezone, while `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`. The same-day match therefore depends on the process TZ. I found no TZ pinning in the repository config.

findings.title: dayjs.tz runs for every override on every slot
findings.body: Line 107 calls `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` inside the `find` callback, so for each slot it runs once for every override in the schedule, before the same-day filter at line 109. getUserAvailability.ts:215-224 maps every dated availability row without a date-range filter, so the count is not bounded by the request window. Filtering to same-day overrides before computing the offset would avoid most of this work.
findings.originReason: This line was added by this diff.

verification.reason: `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` runs for every override inside the `find` on every slot, before the same-day filter. getUserAvailability maps all dated rows without a date-range filter, so the count is not bounded by the request window.

findings.title: The new timezone assertion covers one override per day and nothing else
findings.body: The new block at lines 788-804 covers one override with a single invitee timezone. It does not cover: two override ranges on one day, split working hours, a busy booking on an override day, or an override that crosses midnight in the invitee's zone. Each of these is a failure described in the findings above. The `IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride` fixture (lines 107-129) also gives its override row `days: [0..6]` (lines 119-126), and packages/lib/availability.ts:78 treats any row with days as recurring. On non-override days, that fixture would make the new working-hours check reject every slot. The fixture is only exercised on the override date, so this does not fail today.

verification.reason: The new test only checks one override range with one extra invitee timezone. It does not cover split overrides, split working hours, busy times on override days, or a crossing of midnight. The fixture's override row also has days [0..6], so it is treated as recurring. That gives two working-hours entries per day, but on non-override days only slots before 08:30 UTC would be rejected, not every slot as the finding says.

findings.title: `override.start.toString()` round-trip and an optional `timeZone` that falls back silently
findings.body: Lines 212-213 build dayjs objects from `override.start.toString()`, which drops milliseconds and has no effect beyond `dayjs(override.start)`. The `timeZone` field on the override is optional (packages/types/schedule.d.ts:5), so if it is ever undefined, `.tz(override.timeZone)` falls back to whatever dayjs does with an undefined zone, which I did not verify. Make the field required on the override type, or guard it explicitly.
findings.originReason: These lines were added by this diff.

verification.reason: `override.start.toString()` is a needless round-trip through a string. `timeZone` is optional on TimeRange, so `.tz(undefined)` would silently use dayjs's default zone. Today the only caller, getSchedule, always sets it from availability.timeZone, so this is a cleanup or robustness point only.

contracts.action: Fixed-host slot check now runs override and working-hours checks before the busy check, via checkIfIsAvailable
contracts.before_after: Before: checkIfIsAvailable only ran the seat check and the busy check. After: the override block (105-131) and working-hours block (138-151) run first, and the busy check (153) is skipped on any day that has an override (133-135).
contracts.visible_effect: Slots on override days ignore bookings and calendar busy time. Days with split working hours show no slots.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. No error is raised; slots are either shown when they should be hidden or hidden when they should be shown.

contracts.action: Loose-host slot check runs the same new checks through the spread of the per-user schedule
contracts.before_after: Before: only the busy check ran. After: the same override and working-hours gates as the fixed-host path, because `...userSchedule` carries workingHours and dateOverrides.
contracts.visible_effect: Round-robin and other loose hosts with split hours or override-day busy times are affected in the same way as fixed hosts.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. A host is removed from slot.userIds, and the slot disappears when no host remains.

contracts.action: Reserved-slot branch calls checkIfIsAvailable with only busy and organizerTimeZone
contracts.before_after: Before: the busy check only. After: the same, plus an organizerTimeZone argument that has no effect without dateOverrides or workingHours.
contracts.visible_effect: The override and working-hours rules apply only when the event type has no reservations at all (selectedSlots is empty), so the result depends on other people's reservations.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent inconsistency between the reserved and unreserved branches.

contracts.action: getSlots converts date overrides into invitee-local minutes with a timezone offset
contracts.before_after: Before: minutes were the UTC hour and minute of override.start, with no timezone shift. After: the start and end are shifted by inviteeOffset minus organizerOffset, then the hour and minute are taken from the shifted instant. The day comes from the unshifted instant (line 207), so the day overflow from the shift is dropped.
contracts.visible_effect: The override time is right for same-day overrides. For overrides that cross midnight in the invitee's zone, the slot lands on the wrong invitee day.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. A slot is moved to another day or dropped.

contracts.action: getSchedule carries each host's timeZone onto the flattened date overrides
contracts.before_after: Before: overrides had only userId. After: they also carry timeZone, which getUserAvailability returns at line 228 and computes at line 201.
contracts.visible_effect: None directly; the value is used only by the offset in packages/lib/slots.ts:212.
contracts.failure_mode: If timeZone is undefined, .tz(undefined) in packages/lib/slots.ts:212 falls back to a zone that dayjs chooses, silently.
contracts.open_question: Can the user's timeZone be null, so that the schedule, event type and user zones are all empty and availability.timeZone is undefined?
candidates: the User model's timeZone field in the Prisma schema

contracts.action: organizerTimeZone is computed once before the loop and passed to getTimeSlots
contracts.before_after: Before: the same expression was evaluated inside the call. After: it is hoisted. The value is identical.

summary: The timezone work in getSlots (packages/lib/slots.ts) is right for the case the new test covers, but it places overrides that cross midnight in the invitee's zone on the wrong day. The larger problem is checkIfIsAvailable in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts, which this PR now runs for fixed and loose hosts. Three blockers: an early return on override days skips the busy check, so booked slots show as available; two override ranges on one day reject every slot that day; and split working hours reject every slot on that weekday, because the slot end is never checked. The new test covers a single override only and none of these cases. The snapshot contains no ADRs. I did not run any code.
